authoredFrom: SOL-17 — applied modifiers as `decorators`. Authored 2026-09-30 from the analyzer's measured output. 188 of 5,976 corpus symbols carry applied modifiers across 40 distinct names (`onlyOwner`, `initializer`, `whenNotPaused`).
note: Published on the `decorators` FIELD, not as a relationship — the family contract. C#, Java and F# all treat decorators as metadata on the thing they decorate, and the `modifier_invocation` case already emits the one edge that does carry meaning: a `calls` edge, because invoking a modifier IS calling it. Pinned separately here: `declaredOnly` is a DECLARED modifier with nothing applying it, so it must carry no decorators — a rule that treated any modifier name in scope as applied would attach all three to every function. `untouched` is the bare case. `withOverride` carries BOTH an applied modifier and an `override_specifier`, which are different node types and must not be conflated. The ABSENT case for `decorators` is pinned by `solidity/modifiers-every-scope` rather than by a fixture row: a rule that attached every modifier in the enclosing contract instead of the ones on THIS function would turn `single`'s list into `["onlyOwner","nonReentrant"]`, which `expectSymbols` states exactly. A `"decorators": "not null"` row was written first and removed — the harness has no such spelling, and inventing one inside a fixture would have made the row read as coverage while asserting nothing.

expectRelationships.comment: Relabelled from the pre-relabel `calls` pin: an applied modifier is `decorates` (one site, one label). `onlyOwner` resolves to the `modifier_definition` in `Guarded`, so the application decorates `single`.
Applied modifiers AND an `override_specifier` are different node types and must not be conflated; the override pin lives in external-override-sol11.

forbidRelationships.comment: A DECLARED modifier is not an APPLYING one. Nothing in this file invokes `declaredOnly`, so no edge may exist — the failure mode of a rule that treated every modifier name in the file as applied everywhere.
`single` applies only `onlyOwner`. A rule that collected all modifiers in the enclosing contract rather than the ones on THIS function would add this edge.

THE RELABEL'S OWN FORBID ROW. A modifier application that resolves to a `modifier_definition` is `decorates`, never `calls`. This is what makes a revert of the label move go red — and a widening that emits BOTH edges red too.
Same relabel forbid, second application site, so the second application cannot silently revert independently of the first.
A DECLARED modifier with nothing applying it decorates nothing. The failure mode of a rule that treated every modifier name in scope as applied everywhere.
`single` applies only `onlyOwner`. A rule that collected all modifiers of the enclosing contract rather than the ones on THIS function would add this edge.
